chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskhan, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked him about a man who does not wake up from the last part of the night until ten or fifteen hours have passed for that purpose; should he pray the first prayer (of the night) or make it up? He said, 'No, rather making it up is more beloved to me, for I dislike that he should make that a habit.' And Zurarah used to say, 'How can a prayer be made up if its time had not yet entered? Its time is only after the middle of the night.'

key_terms.آخِرِ اللَّيْلِ: the last part of the night
key_terms.أَوَّلَ اللَّيْلِ: the first part of the night / early night

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for making up the night prayer if one sleeps through its time?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Imam’s preference for *Qada* (making up) over immediate performance to prevent the negligence of sleeping through the prayer from becoming a permanent habit (*khuluq*). Zurarah’s technical nuance regarding the start time of *Salat al-Layl* (after midnight) introduces a jurisprudential debate on whether the prayer is performed within its original time or as a makeup, reflecting the Shia emphasis on balancing ritual precision with practical spiritual discipline.
